body:
## What is the difference between a gross and net lease?

In general, a gross rent quote includes an allowance for some building outgoings, while a net quote separates base rent from additional outgoings. The label alone does not establish every inclusion, adjustment or responsibility in your proposed lease.

For a Newcastle or Hunter business, start with the written terms and cost schedules. Your solicitor should clarify the actual obligations and applicable rules. Do not assume that a net lease makes the roof your responsibility, or that a gross lease fixes every occupancy cost.

## Request a written inclusions schedule

Ask for the proposed rent, available outgoings information, relevant review arrangements and stated exclusions. Identify the period, floor-area basis, GST treatment and source of each figure. Keep proposed, estimated and documented items visibly separate.

| Item | Question to resolve | Useful record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quoted rent | What period, area and inclusions does it cover? | Proposed terms and rent schedule |
| Outgoings | Which costs are proposed, how are they allocated and can they change? | Available budget, statements and lease references |
| Utilities and services | What is included and what needs a separate arrangement? | Written inclusions and supplier inputs |
| Maintenance | Who is responsible for the actual items and activities? | Solicitor clarification and site information |
| Reviews and adjustments | What mechanism, dates and assumptions apply? | Relevant wording and labelled scenarios |
| Parking and access | What is included and what conditions or extra charges are proposed? | Site-specific arrangements |
| End of lease | Which obligations need scope and cost inputs? | Documents, condition records and adviser questions |

**Helpful tip:** use the same schedule for each property. An empty cell should remain a question to resolve, not become an assumed inclusion.

## Gross rent does not replace a scope check

Ask which outgoings are included in the quote, whether any adjustments or exclusions are proposed and which services the business must arrange separately. Review the actual wording with your solicitor rather than treating the word gross as a guarantee of total cost certainty.

Record the business's other occupancy costs alongside the rent comparison. Initial works, furniture, moving, technology and existing lease exit work still need their own scope and budget assumptions.

## Net rent does not settle who pays for everything

Ask which additional amounts are proposed, their basis and the information supporting them. Have your solicitor clarify recoverability and responsibilities for the actual lease and premises, including any relevant retail lease requirements.

Do not use single, double or triple net as a substitute for that review. Maintenance, repair, replacement and building-condition questions need specific documents and appropriate specialist assessment.

**Helpful tip:** separate a solicitor's clarification of responsibility from a contractor's assessment of condition or estimate of work. Both can be needed before a useful budget is approved.

## Compare on one consistent basis

Use the same period, categories and assumptions for each option. Identify which figures include incentives already and which remain estimates. Do not compare a base-rent figure with another proposal's wider occupancy total as though the inclusions were identical.

An incentive-adjusted rent average can be one input, but it does not establish total occupancy cost or decide which space works best for the business. Keep actual payment timing and project expenditure visible, and avoid deducting the same incentive twice.

## Check the actual Newcastle property

Assess the business's activities, staff and visitor access, services, layout and operating requirements at the particular premises. A suburb or building type does not establish suitability, maintenance condition or an appropriate cost allowance.

Ask the appointed advisers to assess any proposed changes, landlord requirements and relevant approval pathway. Connect those inputs to the workplace brief before relying on an opening or move date.

## Questions clients ask

### Is a gross lease always cheaper or safer?

The label does not determine that. Compare written inclusions, actual responsibilities, review assumptions, the premises and the business's requirements with your advisers.

### Does a net lease mean the tenant pays for the roof and air conditioning replacement?

Do not assume so from the label. Ask your solicitor to clarify the relevant wording and rules, and obtain appropriate site and specialist inputs for any identified work.

### Can we use a standard Newcastle outgoings rate?

This guide does not provide a verified market rate. Request the actual proposed costs and supporting information, then record uncertainty and obtain advice before relying on the budget.

### Can YOS compare a renewal with other premises?

YOS can discuss the tenant-side brief, commercial comparison and negotiation scope. The agreed engagement determines the work; savings or particular terms are not guaranteed.

## Sources and their scope

NSW Small Business Commissioner guidance discusses leasing costs in a retail context. Ask your solicitor which requirements apply to your premises; retail rules should not be assumed to apply to every office or industrial lease.

The Queensland source explains gross and net recovery concepts, but its Queensland legal rules are not presented here as NSW advice.
